newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ford German units hit by sick-pay protests.
newsitem.headline: Ford German units hit by sick-pay protests.

text.p: About 21,000 workers at the German unit of U.S. car maker Ford Motor Co were expected to attend protests on Tuesday against changes that took effect on Tuesday in sick-pay benefits under a new law.
Wilfried Kuckelkorn, the leader of Ford's works council, said about 12,000 workers at Ford operations in Cologne participated in a protest on Tuesday morning.
Another 9,000 workers at plants throughout Germany were expected to participate in demonstrations against the new law and for Ford to explain its position on the issue, he said.
The new law calls for workers to receive 80 percent of their gross pay during sick leave, a cut from the prior 100 percent level.
In addition to Ford's German headquarters in Cologne, protests were planned for factories in Berlin, Saarlouis, Wuelfrath, Merkenich and Dueren.
